issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a no-argument messageOnRide() (UML and instructions show messageOnRide(): String and the template Main calls r.messageOnRide() with no parameters), but the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and implementations in Pig and Seal accept a String parameter. This parameter mismatch conflicts with the specified design and the template usage and will confuse students or cause compilation/signature mismatches when following the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable interface and its implementations use a no-argument messageOnRide() to match the UML and template usage (returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"). Alternatively, if an equipment parameter is required pedagogically, update the problem statement, UML, and template Main to document and use messageOnRide(String equipment) consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement (and the provided template Main) define the Rideable interface method as messageOnRide() with no parameters (UML and example calls), but the solution repository implements Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and updates Pig and Seal to use that parameter. This mismatch in the method signature for the same conceptual operation (riding an animal) creates a direct mapping/confusion: students will implement/expect a zero-argument method as described in the exercise and used in the template Main, while the solution uses a different API. This will cause compilation or behavioral inconsistencies and increases extraneous cognitive load.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Rideable API across artifacts. Either (A) remove the 'equipment' parameter from the solution: change Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) to messageOnRide() and update Pig and Seal implementations to implement the no-arg method returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", or (B) update the problem statement and template Main to declare and call messageOnRide(String equipment) (and document the equipment parameter) so all artifacts consistently use the parameterized signature. Option A is recommended to match the original UML and template usage.
